//: Self-contained check that typing looks and records correctly — no app, no network, no account. It loads an inline page with a plain input AND a contenteditable composer, types into both, and asserts each really received the text. Run it after changing anything about input handling.
//why: Two things must hold in the recording. The text must appear character by character (not materialise in one frame), and DemoTape's zoom must HOLD on the field and FOLLOW the caret for the whole sentence. The zoom is driven by clicks and keys, so the driver clicks near the left of the field (where the caret is) and reports typing activity — with the caret's position — while the browser enters the text. Afterwards, check the recording's .source/*.events.json: `clicks` should be 2, `keys` roughly the character count, and the `keys[].x` values must INCREASE across each run. A constant x means the caret measurement is blind again.
//contenteditable: The second scene is the regression that mattered. A contenteditable div has no `.value`, so measuring `el.value` reported a caret offset of zero for every keystroke: the recording passed every assertion while the camera sat on the left edge of the field and the sentence grew away out of frame. Most real chat composers are contenteditable, so this case is the norm, not an edge. See caret.mjs and test-caret.mjs.
